question.text: A company has a paid-up capital of Rs. 200 crore and free reserves of Rs. 300 crore on a standalone basis. On a consolidated basis, the figures are Rs. 200 crore and Rs. 250 crore respectively. What is the maximum amount the company can buy back?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Series IX page 221, the maximum buyback is 25% of the aggregate of paid-up capital and free reserves, based on the lower of the standalone or consolidated figures. Standalone: 200 + 300 = Rs. 500 crore. Consolidated: 200 + 250 = Rs. 450 crore. The lower base is Rs. 450 crore, so the maximum buyback is 25% of Rs. 450 crore = Rs. 112.50 crore. The Trap: Rs. 125 crore comes from 25% of the standalone Rs. 500 crore, but the regulation requires using the lower of the standalone and consolidated bases, which is the consolidated Rs. 450 crore figure here. Note: Always compare standalone and consolidated paid-up capital plus free reserves and apply the 25% cap to the lower figure, as set out on page 221.
